repoConflict.title: Conflicts
repoConflict.description: Conflict status overview and per-file resolution (the three-pane merge editor ships later).
repoConflict.empty: No merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert operation is in progress.
repoConflict.emptyHint: Operations that hit conflicts (merge, pull, cherry-pick, revert, rebase) bring the repository here.
repoConflict.allResolved: All conflicts resolved - ready to continue
repoConflict.abortImpact: Aborting undoes all changes this operation made to the worktree and index and moves HEAD back to where it started; a snapshot is created before aborting.
repoConflict.abortDescription: All changes this operation made to the worktree and index will be undone, returning to the state before it started. A snapshot is created automatically and can be restored later.
repoConflict.contentUnavailable: Binary, oversized or non-UTF-8 file; content is not shown

editor.resultLabel: Block result (editable; editing marks it custom)
editor.conflictProgress: {{resolved}} of {{total}} conflicts resolved in this file
editor.markersBody: The result still contains {{count}} git conflict marker lines (<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>). Saving anyway marks the file resolved, but git will treat those markers as plain text.
editor.markersImpact: Leftover markers do not block saving, but they may mean some conflict blocks were not truly resolved.

autoResolved.both: Identical change from both sides (adopted automatically)

editor.context: Context identical on all three sides
editor.binaryNote: Binary or oversized file; the difference cannot be shown. Take one side's version, or delete the file.
editor.deleteBody: The file will be removed from the worktree and the index as the resolution of this conflict.
editor.deleteImpact: Deleting the file cannot be undone from this dialog; the action is written to the audit log and can be traced in the operation history.
editor.selectFile: Pick a conflicted file on the left to start
editor.selectFileHint: Each file opens its own editing view and disappears from the list once resolved.
editor.loadFailed: Failed to load the conflict detail: the file may already be resolved or its path changed.
editor.batchOursTitle: Take ours for every conflict block?
editor.batchTheirsTitle: Take theirs for every conflict block?
editor.batchBody: All {{blocks}} conflict blocks in this file will be replaced with the {{side}} version; manual edits to these blocks are overwritten.
editor.batchImpact: Scope: {{blocks}} conflict blocks; each block becomes the chosen side's original text. Undo can still revert this.
editor.fileOursTitle: Take the whole file from ours?
editor.fileTheirsTitle: Take the whole file from theirs?
editor.fileBody: The worktree file will be overwritten with the chosen side's full version, current edits are lost, and the file is marked resolved.
editor.fileImpact: This overwrites the worktree file and runs git add; unsaved edits are discarded.
editor.blockAria: Conflict {{current}} of {{total}}, ours {{oursLines}} lines, theirs {{theirsLines}} lines
editor.saveHint: Save and mark resolved (Ctrl+S); press Ctrl+Enter to save and continue once every block is resolved

safety.hint: Dangerous operation detected: {{command}}. Consider the graphical safe action (automatic snapshot) instead.
safety.confirmBody: About to run: {{command}}. It may discard uncommitted changes or rewrite history.
safety.confirmImpact: ForgeDesk cannot automatically undo what happens in the terminal (terminal commands bypass the snapshot safety layer); a compensation snapshot, if enabled, only records the state afterwards.

explain.title: Command explainer
explain.snapshotNote: Explanations come from a bundled snapshot and may lag behind the latest git release.

diagnostics.copiedForSearch: Copied - open your browser and paste to search
diagnostics.dangerousBody: The suggested fix ({{rule}}) rewrites remote history: it only overwrites when the remote still points at the state you know (force-with-lease). A snapshot is created first.
diagnostics.dangerousImpact: Afterwards the remote branch points at new commits; a later push by someone else will be rejected. Local state can be rolled back from snapshots.

diff.errorHint: git diff did not return normally. Retry, or inspect the file in a terminal.
diff.noFile: No line-level changes for this file (a mode change, or not yet tracked by git).
diff.truncatedBanner: This file is too large and was truncated; click "Load full diff" to see everything.

binary.title: Binary file
binary.hint: Binary files have no line-level diff; copy the patch or compare with a dedicated tool.

selection.hint: Click a line number to select that line; hold Shift to select a range.
selection.shortcuts: Shortcuts: s stage · u unstage · d discard
selection.truncatedHint: This file was truncated: load the full diff before staging lines.

diff.sheetDescription: Line-level diff view for the file

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Recent application logs (generated locally, never uploaded, sanitized). Copy from here when reporting a problem.
logs.sanitizedNotice: Tokens and passwords are stripped before anything is written.
logs.highlighted: {{count}} line(s) near this error are highlighted.
logs.emptyHint: Log entries appear here once the app has been running for a while.
logs.errorHint: The log file may be unreachable. Retry, or open the log directory directly.

credentials.title: Saved credentials
credentials.description: Tokens and passwords live in the system credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service). The list shows identifiers only; ciphertext never travels back to the UI.
credentials.keyringUnavailable: The system credential store is unavailable, so credentials cannot be saved securely. Reason
credentials.empty: No credentials saved yet. Add an access token here when you need to reach a private repository.
credentials.secretHint: The plaintext goes straight into the system credential store; it never appears in logs, audit records or this screen.
credentials.deleteImpact: The ciphertext is removed from the system credential store, so later network operations will ask for it again. The remote repository and anything already pushed are unaffected.

vault.createDescription: The passphrase derives the encryption key (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM) and the vault file lives in the app data directory. Unlike the system credential store, anyone who can read that file can attack the passphrase offline, so make it long.
vault.unlockDescription: Credentials are kept in an encrypted file; enter the passphrase to unlock them for synchronisation.
vault.forgotWarning: The passphrase is never stored: forgetting it means the credentials inside cannot be recovered (delete the vault and add them again).

ssh.title: SSH keys
ssh.description: Local keys and the current state of ssh-agent, for chasing down "Permission denied (publickey)". Only file names and public keys are read; private keys are never opened.
ssh.noDirectory: No ~/.ssh directory found (SSH may never have been set up here).
ssh.unavailable: Could not take inventory of the local SSH setup: reading the key directory failed, see the logs for details.
ssh.empty: No SSH keys yet. Generate one with ssh-keygen and add the public key to your hosting platform.
ssh.privateOnlyHint: No matching .pub file: regenerate it from the private key with ssh-keygen -y -f <private key path>.

agent.title: ssh-agent
agent.noIdentities: The agent is running but has no keys loaded
agent.noIdentitiesHint: Add one and retry: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519. The agent takes precedence over the files, which is the usual source of confusion.
agent.notRunningHint: Start the agent and load a key first (on Windows this is usually the ssh-agent service being stopped).
agent.unknown: Could not determine the agent state

test.title: Test connection (remote URL)
test.hint: Runs a single git ls-remote: nothing local changes and nothing is written to the remote.

general.densityHint: Compact tightens list and page padding - useful on small screens or to fit more on one screen.
general.storageHint: Settings and repository records live in a SQLite database in the app data directory and survive restarts.
general.watchHint: Watch the repository directory so the app follows changes made in a terminal or editor. When this is off, the app polls every 15 seconds instead.
general.watchDebounceHint: Multiple file changes within this window collapse into a single refresh. Larger is calmer, smaller feels snappier.
general.perfHint: For large repositories with many changed files, trim rendering details automatically: char-level diff highlighting off, fewer diff context lines, and half the history page size. Forced off keeps every detail on large repositories.
general.themeNote: The theme is kept in browser local storage because it must be readable synchronously before the first paint; storing it in the database would cause a flash on startup.
general.loadFailedHint: The local database may be unreachable. Retry, and if it keeps failing check the logs.

advanced.logsPolicy: Logs are written to the app data directory, rotate on both a daily and a 10MB threshold, and are kept for 7 days. Tokens and passwords are stripped before writing, and nothing is ever uploaded.

privacy.summary: Local first: your code is never collected, no usage data is uploaded, there is no AI inference, and credentials live only in the system keychain.
privacy.noTelemetryBody: This version ships no analytics or telemetry SDK and collects no usage data. If self-hosted telemetry is ever added, it will be off by default, switchable at any time, and will preview the fields it would send before you enable it.
privacy.noAiBody: The application performs no model inference and needs no network access for local Git work.
privacy.credentialsBody: Access tokens are stored only in the system credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service); the local database keeps just a reference. SSH private keys are neither copied nor stored.
privacy.logsBody: Logs are local files, sanitized before writing, kept for 7 days, and never uploaded automatically. You can view or remove them under Advanced.
privacy.requestsBody: Only when you use them: your Git remotes, the hosting API you configured, the update manifest address, and proxy connectivity tests you start yourself. Request headers carry no identity information beyond what authentication requires.
privacy.dataBody: Repository list, settings, audit records and snapshot metadata live in a database inside the app data directory. Uninstalling or clearing that directory removes them; your repositories are untouched.

update.title: Updates
update.autoCheckHint: Checks once at startup. When off, nothing is checked automatically. The check fetches one manifest and carries no personal information.
update.channelHint: The update channel is decided by the build you installed (stable / beta); switching it in-app is not supported yet.

appearance.themeHint: Applies immediately and is remembered; System follows the OS appearance.
appearance.languageHint: Text updates immediately — no restart needed.
appearance.themesHint: Pick a built-in theme or import a custom theme JSON. Each theme belongs to a light or dark appearance.
appearance.themesImportHint: Pick a .json file; colors you omit inherit the built-in values for that appearance.
appearance.themesErrorNotAnObject: The theme must be a JSON object.
appearance.themesErrorInvalidId: The id allows lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only.
appearance.themesErrorInvalidAppearance: appearance must be light or dark.
appearance.themesErrorInvalidVersion: version must be a semantic version (e.g. 1.0.0).
appearance.themesErrorInvalidSizeScale: The size scale must be between 0.8 and 1.5.
appearance.themesDeleteConfirm: Delete theme "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.
appearance.themesDeleteImpact: "{{name}}" is removed from the gallery; if it was active, the built-in palette for its appearance is restored.

audit.title: Operation history
audit.hint: Every write operation (staging, committing, restoring, pruning…) leaves a record: time, result, duration and the linked snapshot. Everything stays on this machine.
audit.loadFailed: Could not read the operation history
audit.loadFailedHint: The local database may be unreachable. Retry.
audit.empty: No records yet. Stage or commit something and it will show up here.

retention.hint: Records beyond either limit are pruned automatically at startup; pruning is itself recorded.

accounts.title: Hosting platform accounts
accounts.description: Which hosting platform identity you are signed in with. Tokens live in the system credential store and are never shown here.
accounts.empty: No account has been signed in yet.
accounts.listError: Failed to load the account list.
accounts.removeDescription: The matching token for {{host}} will be deleted from the credential store and the account record removed from this machine. This cannot be undone.
accounts.loginTitle: Sign in to a hosting platform
accounts.loginDescription: Device code sign-in is recommended; you can also paste a personal access token (PAT).
accounts.deviceIntro: The next step shows a device code: enter it on the GitHub authorization page in your browser, and the app will wait for you automatically.
accounts.stepOpenLink: Step 2: open the authorization page in your browser and enter the code
accounts.waitingHint: Step 3: waiting for authorization (checked about every {{interval}} seconds; restart if it expires).
accounts.waitingFailed: Authorization did not complete. You can request a new device code and try again.
accounts.removeImpact: After removal, the token for this account on {{host}} is deleted from this machine's credential store, and the app will no longer access it as {{login}}.

levelHint.hint: A non-blocking banner appears when a dangerous command is detected and the command still runs; every recognized command is written to the operation history.
levelHint.confirm: High-risk commands require confirmation before they reach the terminal; cancelling sends Ctrl+C to abort the line.

terminal.autoSnapshot: Create a compensation snapshot after dangerous commands
terminal.boundaryNote: Capability boundary: nothing executed in the terminal is guaranteed to be recoverable. A compensation snapshot is only an after-the-fact reference point and cannot undo terminal commands; use the graphical equivalents when you need rollback guarantees.
terminal.historyEmpty: No diagnoses yet. Once an error matches a rule, the last 20 are listed here.

shortcuts.recording: Press the new key combination (Esc to cancel)…
shortcuts.clickToRecord: Click to record a new shortcut

presetHint.default: Balanced: file tree plus the detail panel on the right.
presetHint.review: Detail panel docked to the bottom for more horizontal diff space.
presetHint.editor: Editor mode: narrower file tree for focused editing.

layout.importInvalid: Clipboard does not contain valid layout JSON; nothing applied.
layout.corruptedToast: The saved layout was corrupted and has been reset to default.
layout.corruptedInline: The saved layout was invalid and fell back to default (adjust and save again below).

snapshots.title: Snapshots and rollback
snapshots.description: A snapshot is taken automatically before each commit; go back to that point when something goes wrong.
snapshots.emptyHint: After the first commit, a "pre-commit" snapshot appears here.
snapshots.restoreConfirmDescription: This returns to the state where HEAD was {{oid}}.
snapshots.impactUnknown: The difference between the current state and the snapshot could not be read. Close and retry.
snapshots.impactRefMissing: This snapshot's anchor is gone; it cannot be restored.
snapshots.impactUnchanged: The working tree, index and HEAD already match the snapshot; nothing to restore.
snapshots.impactHead: HEAD will move from {{current}} back to {{oid}}.
snapshots.impactIndex: The index will also be restored to the snapshot's tree; staged but uncommitted content will be dropped.
snapshots.impactUntracked: Untracked files: the ones with a content backup are written back, the rest stay as they are.
snapshots.impactRestorable: {{count}} untracked file(s) will be written back (missing now, or their content changed).
snapshots.impactMissing: {{count}} untracked file(s) were never backed up; a restore cannot bring them back.
snapshots.impactExtra: The {{count}} extra untracked file(s) present now will not be deleted.
snapshots.createdWithWarning: The snapshot was created, but it does not contain all untracked content:

warning.untrackedBackupSkipped: This snapshot excludes {{count}} untracked file(s) ({{size}} total, over the {{limit}} limit); a restore will not bring them back.
warning.untrackedBackupPartial: {{count}} untracked file(s) could not be backed up ({{detail}}); a restore will not bring them back.
warning.backupDirUnavailable: The snapshot backup directory is unavailable ({{detail}}); this snapshot has no untracked content.
warning.spaceReclaimed: To free space, {{count}} old snapshot(s) were removed ({{size}} freed).
warning.orphansRemoved: Removed {{count}} leftover backup directory(ies) from an earlier run.

report.title: Restore report
report.head: HEAD restored ({{oid}})
report.verified: Verified (HEAD / index / backup content match byte for byte)
report.unverified: Some content did not pass verification; see the entries below
report.failed: {{count}} untracked file(s) could not be restored: {{paths}}
report.extra: The {{count}} extra untracked file(s) present now were not deleted: {{paths}}

outcome.rolledBack: Restore failed; rolled back to the pre-restore state
outcome.emergency: Restore failed and could not roll back: manual recovery required

stage.head: Restore HEAD and the working tree

pending.title: An earlier restore did not finish
pending.detail: The restore of snapshot #{{id}} stopped at "{{stage}}" (the app was interrupted). You can continue that restore, or just clear this notice.

emergency.title: Manual recovery required
emergency.commands: Run these in the repository directory (copyable):

operations.title: Operation history
operations.description: Every destructive operation takes a snapshot first; this is where you see them and can go back.
operations.error: Failed to load the operation history
operations.emptyHint: After your first commit or destructive operation, its record (and rollback point) appears here.

rollback.title: Go back to before this step?
rollback.description: The snapshot taken by this operation restores the working tree, the index and HEAD.
rollback.impactHead: HEAD will move from {{oid}} back to where snapshot #{{snapshot}} was taken.
rollback.confirmHint: I understand: staged and uncommitted changes will be dropped (untracked files are never deleted).

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: Write the message, then check the exact git command in the preview.
commit.messagePlaceholder: Summarise the change (first line is the subject, keep it under ~72 chars)
commit.bodyPlaceholder: Optional details: why this changed and what it affects
commit.warningSubjectTooLong: The first line is long (keep it under ~{{max}} chars); it will be truncated in lists.
commit.amendHint: Fold the current content into the last commit and replace its message.
commit.signOffHint: Append a Signed-off-by line (required by DCO workflows).
commit.noVerifyHint: Do not run pre-commit / commit-msg and friends. Only tick this when you know the consequences.
commit.recentEmpty: This repository has no commits yet.
commit.stagedNoneHint: A commit contains only what is staged. Stage files or lines in the working tree first.
commit.previewDescription: This is exactly what will happen; it runs as soon as you confirm.
commit.previewHooksEmpty: This repository has no runnable commit hooks
commit.previewSnapshot: A snapshot is created automatically once the commit succeeds — roll back anytime from the Snapshots page.
commit.previewAmend: This rewrites the last commit; if it is already pushed, pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendEmpty: This repository has no commits yet, so there is nothing to amend.
commit.amendPushedWarning: This commit may already exist on a remote ({{refs}}). Rewriting it diverges local from remote; pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendPushedUnknown: This commit may already exist on a remote. Rewriting it diverges local from remote; pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendModeIncludeHint: Fold the staged content into the last commit (the git default).
commit.amendModeMessageOnlyHint: Replace the message only; staged content stays in the index and is not committed.
commit.hooksPhaseCodeCheck: Looks like a code check (the usual pre-commit shape)
commit.hooksPhaseMessageCheck: Looks like a commit-message check (the commit-msg stage)
commit.hooksPhaseDependencies: Looks like a dependency installation failure
commit.hooksPhaseUnknown: The output does not say which hook failed
commit.hooksListEmpty: This repository has no hooks installed.
commit.hooksListNotExecutable: Missing the execute bit, so git ignores it

clean.title: Working tree is clean
clean.hint: No uncommitted changes; edit files or pull and they will show up here.

error.title: Could not read the working tree status
error.hint: The repository may be unreachable. Retry, or reopen the repository.

workspace.largeChange: A large number of files changed (for example a branch switch); the list was refreshed.

discard.title: Discard these changes?
discard.description: The following changes will be lost and cannot be restored by this app:
discard.linesDescription: The selected lines in this file will be reverted. Staged content is not affected.

branches.title: Branches & tags
branches.createHint: Create a new branch from the current HEAD.
branches.deleteMergedHint: This branch is merged; its commits remain reachable from history.
branches.deleteUnmergedWarning: This branch has {{ahead}} commits of its own; force-deleting makes them unreachable (a snapshot is taken first):
branches.switchHint: The working tree has uncommitted changes; choose what to do with them:
branches.switchStash: Stash changes and restore after switching (recommended)
branches.switchForce: Discard all uncommitted changes (irreversible; a snapshot is taken first)
branches.tagHint: Leave the message empty for a lightweight tag; fill it for an annotated one.
branches.error: Failed to load branches and tags
branches.quickCreate: Type a name; Enter creates and switches

merge.title: Merge branches
merge.hint: Preview what this merge will do before executing it. The preview never touches the worktree.
merge.upToDate: The current branch already contains every commit of that branch; nothing to do.
merge.willFastForward: Fast-forward: the current branch will advance to the {{count}} incoming commit(s).
merge.willMergeCommit: A merge commit will be created ({{count}} incoming commit(s) merged in).
merge.conflictPreview: The preview found conflicts; executing will stop at the conflict state:
merge.previewUnavailable: The local git is too old to preview conflicts; if any appear, the merge will stop at the conflict state.
merge.messageLabel: Merge message (used when a merge commit is created)

sync.fetchHint: Updates remote-tracking refs only; the local branch and worktree stay untouched
sync.pullHint: Fetches the upstream and merges it into the current branch (a snapshot is taken first)
sync.pushHint: Pushes the current branch to its upstream
sync.noUpstream: This branch has no upstream yet
sync.aheadTip: Commits this branch is ahead of upstream
sync.behindTip: Commits this branch is behind upstream

conflict.title: The pull produced conflicts
conflict.impact: The repository is left in a conflicted merge state: every conflicted file must be resolved before you can commit or push again. A snapshot was taken before this pull, so you can always roll back.

rejected.title: Push rejected
rejected.impact: The remote has commits you do not have. Fetching first is the safe path; if you must overwrite, use force-with-lease (git only overwrites when the remote still points at the commit you last saw).

lease.title: Overwrite the remote?
lease.impact: This comparison was just fetched: this branch is {{ahead}} commits ahead and {{behind}} commits behind. Overwriting rewrites the remote branch to your local history, so the commits you are behind will not be on it (they remain recoverable on the hosting platform).
lease.description: The latest state of {{upstream}} was fetched; this comparison is what the overwrite is based on.

stash.title: Stashes
stash.nothingToStash: Nothing to stash: the worktree is clean.
stash.untrackedFiles: Untracked files (stored separately in the third parent)
stash.conflict: Applying the stash produced {{count}} conflicts: the repository is in a conflicted state.
stash.emptyHint: When changes should be neither committed nor lost, stash them and take them back any time.
stash.dropImpact: The stash disappears from this list for good. The underlying commits remain recoverable by oid until git collects them - there will be no further prompt.
stash.dropRecoverHint: Dropped oids are written to the audit history and can be recovered until git collects them.
stash.clearImpact: All {{count}} stashes will be dropped and cannot be restored from this list.
stash.branchTitle: Create a branch from this stash
stash.branchHint: The branch starts at the stash's base and applies its contents - the regular way out of an 'apply conflict', and it cannot conflict with your worktree.
stash.branchImpact: Creates a new branch and switches to it; the current branch and the rest of your worktree are untouched.

historyOps.title: Commit actions
historyOps.pickHint: Select a commit in the graph to see the actions available for it.

reflog.title: Recent ref movements (reflog)
reflog.recoverHint: Creates a new branch at {{oid}}: no existing branch moves and nothing is checked out.
reflog.recoverImpact: Only a new branch pointing at that commit is created; the current branch, the index and the worktree are untouched.

resetPlan.title: Reset plan ({{mode}})
resetPlan.impact: {{count}} of the {{total}} commits being discarded exist nowhere but this machine - afterwards only a snapshot or the reflog can bring them back.
resetPlan.description: Resets to "{{subject}}", discarding the {{discarded}} commits after it.
resetPlan.lostStaged: Staged changes will be discarded: {{count}} files.
resetPlan.lostWorktree: Worktree changes will be discarded: {{count}} files.
resetPlan.confirmationPrompt: Type "{{word}}" to confirm (this is the last confirmation)

history.title: History
history.description: Browse the commit graph: branches, merges and refs at a glance.

empty.title: No commits yet
empty.hint: This repository has no commit history to show; the graph appears after the first commit.

emptyFiltered.title: No matching commits
emptyFiltered.description: No commit matches the current filters; clear the filters to see the full history.

error.title: Failed to load commit history
error.hint: The repository may be unreachable; retry, or reopen the repository.

rebase.title: Organize commit history
rebase.description: Reorder the commits in {{base}}…{{head}}: drag to reorder, or change a single commit's action.
rebase.loadFailed: Failed to load the range commits (the repository may have changed).
rebase.cannotOrganize: Cannot organize: include an older commit as well (the oldest selected commit needs a parent as the starting point).
rebase.stepListHint: Drag to reorder; or focus a row and press Alt+↑/↓ to move it

reason.squashAsFirst: There is no earlier commit to merge into
reason.squashOnMerge: A merge commit cannot be squashed (the merge structure would be lost)
reason.allDropped: Keep at least one commit, or use reset instead
reason.oidOutsideRange: This commit is outside the reorganization range

rebase.newMessage: New commit message (leave empty to keep the original)

preview.pushed: The range contains pushed commits; pushing afterwards needs force-with-lease.
preview.blocked: The plan has invalid actions; fix them to see the preview.

rebase.pausedConflict: Paused: conflicts need to be resolved
rebase.pausedEdit: Paused: edit the content, then continue
rebase.snapshotHint: A snapshot #{{id}} was created before the rewrite; you can roll back from the snapshots page.
rebase.noSnapshot: No snapshot could be created — check the snapshots page for an available rollback point before relying on it.

confirm.title: Confirm history rewrite

push-non-fast-forward.title: Push rejected: the remote has new commits
push-non-fast-forward.explanation: The remote branch is ahead of your local record; pushing as-is would discard someone else's work, so Git refused.
push-non-fast-forward.cause1: The remote branch contains commits you do not have locally (someone pushed first).

push-no-upstream.title: Branch has no upstream
push-no-upstream.explanation: This branch has not been linked to a remote branch yet, so Git does not know where to push.
push-no-upstream.cause1: A newly created branch is not linked to a remote branch yet.

push-fetch-first.title: Push rejected: fetch first
push-fetch-first.explanation: The remote branch is newer; Git asks you to fetch and integrate first.
push-fetch-first.cause1: The remote has new commits to integrate before pushing.

push-stale-lease.title: Force-with-lease rejected: stale info
push-stale-lease.explanation: The safe force push detected the remote moved past your local knowledge - the protection working as intended. Fetch, verify, then retry.
push-stale-lease.cause1: The remote updated after your last fetch; the local record is stale.

push-remote-rejected.title: Remote rejected the push
push-remote-rejected.explanation: The push was rejected by the remote server (not local Git), typically by branch protection or a server-side hook.
push-remote-rejected.cause1: The remote server (not local Git) rejected the push, commonly branch protection or a server hook.

push-permission-403.title: Push rejected: no permission
push-permission-403.explanation: The current account lacks push access to this repository (403).
push-permission-403.cause1: The current account lacks push access to this repository.

net-dns-failure.title: Could not resolve host
net-dns-failure.explanation: DNS lookup failed - check the network, proxy, or the remote URL spelling.
net-dns-failure.cause1: DNS lookup failed: network down, DNS misconfigured, or a typo in the URL.

net-connection-refused.title: Connection refused
net-connection-refused.explanation: The TCP connection was refused by the peer or an intermediate device.
net-connection-refused.cause1: Nothing listens on the target port, or a firewall/proxy intercepted the connection.

net-timeout.title: Connection timed out
net-timeout.explanation: Waiting for the peer timed out.
net-timeout.cause1: The network is slow or down; large clones are especially prone to timeouts.

net-ssl-certificate.title: TLS certificate verification failed
net-ssl-certificate.explanation: The HTTPS certificate is not trusted - the connection works, the certificate chain is the problem.
net-ssl-certificate.cause1: Expired or self-signed server certificate, or a corporate proxy re-signing the chain.

net-proxy-failure.title: Proxy unavailable
net-proxy-failure.explanation: The proxy connection failed: missing credentials, proxy down, or misconfigured.
net-proxy-failure.cause1: The proxy needs credentials, refused the connection, or is misconfigured.

net-auth-failed.title: Authentication failed
net-auth-failed.explanation: The remote rejected the credentials: the token may be expired, revoked, or lacking scopes.
net-auth-failed.cause1: The username or token is invalid or expired.

net-prompts-disabled.title: Cannot prompt for credentials
net-prompts-disabled.explanation: Git runs non-interactively and this operation needs a username/password - save a credential in settings first.
net-prompts-disabled.cause1: Git runs non-interactively and no saved credential is available.

net-could-not-read-remote.title: Could not read from remote repository
net-could-not-read-remote.explanation: The connection was established but reading the repository failed - credentials or permissions.
net-could-not-read-remote.cause1: The SSH/HTTPS channel failed: credentials, network, or repository permissions.

ssh-publickey-denied.title: SSH public key rejected
ssh-publickey-denied.explanation: The server did not accept your SSH public key.
ssh-publickey-denied.cause1: The server rejected the SSH public key: not uploaded, agent not loaded, or the wrong key.

ssh-host-key-verification.title: Host key verification failed
ssh-host-key-verification.explanation: The host is not in known_hosts, so SSH refused to continue - verify the fingerprint and trust it.
ssh-host-key-verification.cause1: First connection to this host; its fingerprint is not trusted yet (missing from known_hosts).
ssh-host-key-verification.fix_trust_host: Verify and trust the host fingerprint

remote-not-a-repo.title: Remote is not a git repository
remote-not-a-repo.explanation: The address connects but is not a Git repository - check the URL.
remote-not-a-repo.cause1: The remote URL is wrong or does not point at a Git repository.

wt-not-a-repo.title: Not a git repository
wt-not-a-repo.explanation: Git found no .git in the given directory or any parent.
wt-not-a-repo.cause1: The target path is not inside a Git repository.

wt-dubious-ownership.title: Dubious ownership
wt-dubious-ownership.explanation: The repository belongs to another user and Git refuses to operate. After verifying it is trusted, add the directory to safe.directory.
wt-dubious-ownership.cause1: The repository directory is owned by another user (Git's safety check).

wt-index-lock.title: Index is locked
wt-index-lock.explanation: An index.lock exists: another Git process is working on this repository. Make sure nothing else is running before removing the lock.
wt-index-lock.cause1: Another git process is writing the index (or a crashed one left the lock behind).
wt-index-lock.fix_close_other_process: How to handle a stale lock safely

wt-local-changes-overwritten.title: Local changes would be overwritten
wt-local-changes-overwritten.explanation: This operation would overwrite uncommitted changes, so Git refused. Stash or commit them first.
wt-local-changes-overwritten.cause1: Uncommitted changes conflict with what is about to be applied.

wt-detached-head.title: Detached HEAD
wt-detached-head.explanation: HEAD points at a commit instead of a branch. Commits made here may become unreachable - create a branch first.
wt-detached-head.cause1: HEAD points at a commit, not a branch; new commits here belong to no branch.
wt-detached-head.fix_create_branch: Create a branch for the current state

wt-filename-too-long.title: Filename too long
wt-filename-too-long.explanation: The path exceeds the system limit (260 characters on Windows by default).
wt-filename-too-long.cause1: The Windows default 260-character path limit (core.longpaths can lift it).

wt-permission-denied-fs.title: Filesystem permission denied
wt-permission-denied-fs.explanation: The operating system refused the write to a file or directory.
wt-permission-denied-fs.cause1: Insufficient filesystem permissions: read-only directory or a file in use.

wt-disk-full.title: Disk full
wt-disk-full.explanation: The write failed because the disk is full - clean up snapshot caches or other large files and retry.
wt-disk-full.cause1: The disk has no space left.

wt-lf-replaced.title: Line endings will be converted
wt-lf-replaced.explanation: This is an autocrlf notice (not an error): LF in the working tree becomes CRLF on commit. Cross-platform teams should agree on a policy.
wt-lf-replaced.cause1: Automatic line-ending conversion (core.autocrlf) turns LF into CRLF on commit.

wt-large-file.title: File exceeds the platform size limit
wt-large-file.explanation: The hosting platform rejected the oversized file - use Git LFS or remove it from history.
wt-large-file.cause1: A single file exceeds the platform limit (100MB for regular GitHub files).

commit-no-identity.title: Missing committer identity
commit-no-identity.explanation: Git does not know who you are (no user.name / user.email). Fill it in once on the commit panel.
commit-no-identity.fix_set_identity: Set your identity on the commit panel

commit-empty-message.title: Empty commit message
commit-empty-message.explanation: Git refuses a commit with an empty message.

commit-nothing.title: Nothing to commit
commit-nothing.explanation: The staging area is empty. Stage some changes first.
commit-nothing.cause1: The staging area is empty (or matches the last commit).

commit-hook-rejected.title: Hook rejected the operation
commit-hook-rejected.explanation: A pre-commit / commit-msg hook failed. Fix what it reports and retry.
commit-hook-rejected.cause1: A repository hook script rejected the operation.

conflict-content.title: Content conflict
conflict-content.explanation: Both sides modified the same region - resolve them in the conflict wizard.
conflict-content.cause1: Both sides modified the same region; Git cannot merge it automatically.

merge-auto-failed.title: Automatic merge failed
merge-auto-failed.explanation: The merge produced conflicts: resolve them, git add, then continue.
merge-auto-failed.cause1: The merge hit conflicts that need manual resolution.

hist-bad-object.title: Bad object
hist-bad-object.explanation: The given hash or reference does not exist in this repository.
hist-bad-object.cause1: The hash or reference is a typo, or the object is not in this repository.

hist-unknown-revision.title: Unknown revision or path
hist-unknown-revision.explanation: The branch/commit/path does not exist locally - a fetch may help.
hist-unknown-revision.cause1: The branch/commit/path is misspelled or not fetched yet.

hist-branch-not-exist.title: Branch does not exist
hist-branch-not-exist.explanation: The branch cannot be found - check the name or whether it was deleted.
hist-branch-not-exist.cause1: No branch with this name exists locally or on the remote.

hist-tag-exists.title: Tag already exists
hist-tag-exists.explanation: A tag with this name already exists.
hist-tag-exists.cause1: A tag with the same name already exists.

hist-branch-exists.title: Branch already exists
hist-branch-exists.explanation: A branch with this name already exists.
hist-branch-exists.cause1: A branch with the same name already exists.

hist-no-tracking-info.title: No tracking information
hist-no-tracking-info.explanation: This branch has no upstream. Set one with --set-upstream so plain pull/push work.
hist-no-tracking-info.cause1: The branch has no upstream, so pull/push has no target.

hist-rebase-in-progress.title: Rebase still in progress
hist-rebase-in-progress.explanation: A rebase is mid-flight: resolve all conflicts, mark them, then continue (or abort).
hist-rebase-in-progress.cause1: A previous rebase is unfinished (conflicts unresolved).

hist-merge-in-progress.title: Merge still in progress
hist-merge-in-progress.explanation: A merge is mid-flight: resolve conflicts and commit, or abort.

hist-shallow-clone.title: Shallow clone
hist-shallow-clone.explanation: This repository was cloned shallow (--depth); the history is incomplete.
hist-shallow-clone.cause1: A shallow clone has incomplete history, limiting some operations.

lfs-not-installed.title: Git LFS not installed
lfs-not-installed.explanation: The repository uses Git LFS but git-lfs is not installed locally.
lfs-not-installed.cause1: git-lfs is not installed, so LFS pointer files cannot be resolved.

lfs-missing-objects.title: LFS object fetch failed
lfs-missing-objects.explanation: Downloading LFS objects failed: network, permission, or server issue.
lfs-missing-objects.cause1: The LFS object server is unreachable or rejected the request.

api-rate-limit.title: API rate limit exceeded
api-rate-limit.explanation: The platform API quota is exhausted. Signing in raises the limit substantially.
api-rate-limit.cause1: The GitHub API quota is exhausted (60 unauthenticated requests/hour).
api-rate-limit.fix_add_account: Sign in to raise the quota

api-bad-credentials.title: Bad API credentials
api-bad-credentials.explanation: The token was rejected: expired or revoked. Sign in again.
api-bad-credentials.cause1: The API token is invalid or was revoked.

submodule-missing.title: Submodule problem
submodule-missing.explanation: A submodule is not initialized or cannot be accessed.
submodule-missing.cause1: A submodule is missing its mapping or was never initialized.

wt-invalid-filename.title: Invalid filename
wt-invalid-filename.explanation: The filesystem rejected this file name.
wt-invalid-filename.cause1: The file name contains characters the filesystem disallows.

wt-crlf-replaced.title: Line endings will be converted
wt-crlf-replaced.explanation: This is an autocrlf notice (not an error): CRLF becomes LF on commit.
wt-crlf-replaced.cause1: Automatic conversion (core.autocrlf=input) turns CRLF into LF on commit.

net-cert-expired.title: Server certificate expired
net-cert-expired.explanation: The peer HTTPS certificate has expired - a server misconfiguration, or a wrong system clock.
net-cert-expired.cause1: The peer HTTPS certificate has expired.

hist-branches-diverged.title: Local and remote have diverged
hist-branches-diverged.explanation: Both histories moved forward - pick a merge or rebase strategy.
hist-branches-diverged.cause1: Both sides have new commits; the integration strategy is unspecified.
